out_of_scope: Interpreter::new_permissive() is an explicit legacy opt-out for trusted integrations. Interpreter::new() is strict during its high-level load/eval/call methods, but direct use of public low-level Env/Value/eval APIs is host-controlled and is not a sandbox boundary.

Capability rows that are checker-only (time::*, uuid v4/v7) or declared-only (ffi, net_internal): enforced at check time / in generated sandbox policy, NOT uniformly runtime-gated. Documented in the P2 capability enforcement scope table.
OS-level sandbox enforcement: seccomp/WASI/egress policy is generated (enforced:false) and applied only on Linux via an external reference harness; macOS/Windows OS sandboxing is named-deferred.
memory::* natives: bridge-only, caps-invisible; outside the capability registry.
WV-5 proves the Wasm build and real Node execution, not live browser-page execution.
tracked_debt: The two enforcement-status scripts are string-presence checks, not behavioral proofs; behavioral evidence is the cargo test suites.
The exact current-truth claim fixture is a copy/metadata regression guard; a semantic caps-claims-as-doctests guard remains a possible strengthening.

The public low-level Interpreter Env/Value/eval surfaces make the strict default an API-path guarantee, not a Rust-host sandbox; the post-acceptance delta review tracks whether that surface should be narrowed.
The VM cross-IR caps recheck has a deterministic trap API but is not yet mandatory on every compile/run entry; the post-acceptance delta review tracks default-path wiring.

current_scope_limits: Interpreter::new_permissive() deliberately permits unframed direct calls for trusted integrations; strict-by-default is not a claim that the opt-out is impossible.

Direct use of the public low-level Env/Value/eval APIs is controlled by the Rust host and can execute outside an Interpreter method's per-instance strict scope; it is not covered as a sandbox boundary.
Capability rows that are checker-only (time::*, uuid v4/v7) or declared-only (ffi, net_internal) are not uniformly runtime-gated.
OS-level sandbox policy is generated with enforced:false and applied only on Linux via the external seccomp reference harness; macOS/Windows OS sandboxing remains named-deferred.
memory::* natives remain bridge-only and caps-invisible.
WV-5 proves the Wasm build and Node execution, not live browser-page execution.
remaining_debt: The behavioral Rust suites remain the authority for runtime enforcement; copy/status fixtures are regression guards, not substitutes for execution tests.
A semantic caps-claims-as-doctests guard remains a possible strengthening beyond the exact current-truth fixture.
The post-acceptance delta review must resolve or explicitly retain the public low-level interpreter bypass surface and the non-default VM cross-IR recheck entry.
The W-PLAY browser adapter, authority-diff surface, under-30-second Playwright path, and live Pages proof remain launch work.
